study.research_problem: Conventional metallic fracture plates can unload bone because their stiffness greatly exceeds that of bone, motivating joint material and topology design of a lower-stiffness plate.
study.exact_gap: The study asks how plate material and prescribed topology volume reduction alter load transfer and a stress-shielding factor in a controlled fracture construct, including whether a heavily reduced PEEK-CF plate remains numerically feasible after geometry is made more printable (S001:C01-S003:C01).
study.objective_or_hypothesis: Compare metallic, functionally graded, and PEEK-CF plates; optimize the selected composite plate at 75%, 50%, and 25% retained volume; reconstruct the preferred geometry for manufacturing constraints; and compare predicted stresses, deformation, and SSF (S003:C01-S008:C02).
study.study_design: Linear-elastic FE study of a simplified cylindrical tibial shaft, transverse fracture and 50%-healed callus, 1 mm locked-plate gap, threadless screws, one 800 N axial load, material variants, three SIMP volume fractions, and an assumed healing-stage material sequence (S004:C01-S008:C02).
study.sample_or_model: One idealized 25 mm-diameter tibia, 103 x 4 mm curved plate, four screw construct, cortical/trabecular bone and callus; no patient geometry, printed plate, cadaver, animal, or clinical sample.
comparators: Steel, titanium, magnesium, Ti-HAP FGM, PEEK-10CF, and PEEK-30CF plate materials
Original PEEK-CF plate versus TOPO75, TOPO50, and TOPO25
Raw TOPO25 versus manually corrected manufacturing-oriented geometry
Stabilized versus non-stabilized bone stress in the SSF formula
TOPO25 versus steel across assumed healing stages
method_spine: Fix a controlled bone-fracture-plate geometry and locked-plate load path.
Declare material axes, constitutive assumptions, healing-state callus properties, contacts, mesh, and axial load.
Compare material alternatives before selecting the topology substrate.
Run prescribed retained-volume SIMP cases under the same model.
Reconstruct thin/critical regions for manufacturing and rerun FE.
Calculate SSF against an explicit unplated reference while keeping it a model surrogate.

verification: A mesh-refinement study reports convergence of average stress at smaller element sizes, although a quantitative acceptance criterion and consistency with the final component-specific mesh sizes are not fully documented (S006:C01; S009:C01).
The manually corrected TOPO25 geometry is rerun under the same FE conditions, verifying preservation of the modeled response after reconstruction (S012:C01).
calibration: Material and healing-stage properties are literature assigned; no specimen-, patient-, or construct-level inverse calibration is performed (S005:C01-S006:C02).
validation: No physical plate, coupon, construct, cadaver, animal, or clinical comparison validates stress, stiffness, fatigue, fracture-gap stability, or the week-by-week SSF curve.
Trend agreement with prior simplified numerical studies is contextual support, not independent experimental validation (S014:C02-S017:C02).
sensitivity: Plate material, retained volume, mesh density, and assumed healing stage are varied (S005:C01-S013:C02).

No sensitivity covers multiaxial/cyclic loads, anatomy, plate gap/contact, screw preload/threads, callus properties, fracture geometry, material uncertainty, optimization filters, or reconstruction rules.
application_prediction: Reduced stress shielding and improved functional recovery are application interpretations of FE surrogates, not measured healing or patient outcomes (S017:C01-S018:C01).

primary_outcomes: Across material models, construct maximum stress was reported around 33 MPa for steel, about 24 MPa for titanium/magnesium, and about 22 MPa for PEEK composite, with small global deformation; component-level directionality is not consistently aligned with the stated stress-shielding objective (S010:C01-S010:C03).

TOPO25 retained 25% of initial material and produced similar modeled bone/plate deformation; reported bone and plate stress changes relative to the original composite geometry were about 6% and 33%, respectively (S011:C01-S011:C03).
After manual wall/critical-region correction, TOPO25 produced a stress map similar to the raw topology output and stresses less than 1 MPa below the original composite-plate construct (S012:C01).

Modeled PEEK-10CF SSF averaged roughly 0.2-0.3 and TOPO25 reduced it further; the assumed healing sequence reached a favorable range earlier than steel and later generated negative SSF, which indicates bone stress above the reference rather than proven beneficial remodeling (S013:C01-S013:C02).
study.highest_evidence_level_reached: Verified comparative FE trends in one simplified axial-load model; no physical manufacturing, construct mechanics, biological healing, or clinical validation.

argument_map.central_claim: Within one idealized axial locked-plate model, lower-stiffness PEEK-CF and aggressive volume reduction alter modeled load sharing and SSF favorably, but optimality, manufacturability, fatigue safety, healing benefit, and clinical recovery are not established.
data: Material-screen FE results, three retained-volume topology cases, one manually reconstructed geometry, mesh study, and SSF calculations over assigned healing properties (S005:C01-S013:C02).
argument_map.warrant: Comparative modeling can isolate material and volume effects under fixed assumptions, but translation requires construct-level stability/failure metrics, manufacturing evidence, and independent biological or clinical endpoints.
backing: The authors explicitly limit interpretation to pure axial loading, cylindrical anatomy, and a selected plate-bone gap/contact configuration (S014:C02-S014:C03).
argument_map.qualifier: Relative FE comparison for the stated geometry, materials, load, contact, and healing assumptions.
rebuttals_or_boundaries: The paper does not fully report the optimization objective, design/non-design domains, penalization/filter, convergence, or constraint values beyond retained volume.
Minimizing plate/bone peak stress, preserving fracture stability, and increasing bone load are distinct objectives whose desired directions may conflict.
Manual geometry correction followed by FE does not demonstrate printability or as-built properties.
One static axial force omits bending, torsion, gait cycles, screw pullout, fatigue, and fracture-gap motion.
The week labels derive from assigned callus properties rather than longitudinal measurement or calibrated healing prediction.
Negative SSF denotes overloading relative to the reference and is not automatically beneficial.

measured: No physical or biological outcome is measured; reported stresses, strains, deformation, SSF, mass/volume, and healing-time curves are numerical outputs.
predicted: FE component stresses/deformations and SSF under one static load, three prescribed topology reductions, corrected geometry, and assigned callus states (S009:C01-S013:C02).
inferred: A more physiological biomechanical environment, reduced resorption/loosening, improved healing, functional recovery, economic benefit, and AM feasibility are inferred from numerical surrogates (S015:C01-S018:C01).
recommended: Report the full optimization contract, quantify raw-to-reconstructed geometry loss, print and inspect specimens, validate static/fatigue/fracture-gap response, and test multiaxial patient/anatomy/healing uncertainty before biological claims.
proxy_to_outcome_bridges: SSF is a model-defined stress ratio, not bone resorption or healing.
Low plate stress does not by itself mean adequate fixation or reduced stress shielding.
Global displacement is not fracture-gap micromotion/strain.
Assigned callus stiffness over nominal weeks is not a validated longitudinal healing model.
A printable-looking solid geometry is not an as-built implant.
overclaim_risks: The conclusion labels composite stiffness optimal and links it to functional recovery without physical or biological validation (S018:C01).
TOPO25 is called most suitable although only one axial model and three volume fractions were evaluated.
Re-analysis after geometric correction is described as manufacturability verification despite no manufacturing evidence (S012:C01).
The automatic experimental-mechanical cue is false; the work is entirely computational.

section_moves.move: Declare the implant-bone load-path model before optimization
section_moves.execution: Geometry, gap, screws, material axes, callus state, mesh, fixation, and axial load are specified before material/topology comparison (S004:C01-S006:C02).
section_moves.transferable_principle: Freeze geometry, materials, contact, loading, healing state, and reference construct before comparing implant materials or topologies.
section_moves.failure_mode: A controlled model supports relative comparison but narrows external validity.

section_moves.move: Write topology optimization as an executable contract
section_moves.execution: Three retained-volume SIMP cases are reported, but objective, filters, stopping rules, and protected regions remain incomplete (S007:C01).
section_moves.transferable_principle: State objective, constraints, design variables, non-design regions, loads/weights, material interpolation, filter, manufacturing bounds, convergence, and selection rule.
section_moves.failure_mode: Prescribed volume alone cannot establish what 'optimal' means or whether the result is reproducible.

section_moves.move: Quantify reconstruction loss after manufacturability editing
section_moves.execution: The raw TOPO25 output is manually corrected and rerun, showing similar modeled fields (S012:C01).
section_moves.transferable_principle: Preserve raw, reconstructed, and as-built states; report geometry/volume and every critical response before and after each transition.
section_moves.failure_mode: Re-analysis verifies only the edited CAD model, not printing or device mechanics.

section_moves.move: Bound a stress-shielding surrogate by its reference and direction
section_moves.execution: SSF is explicitly defined against unplated bone and later negative values are identified as bone stress above reference (S008:C01-S008:C02; S013:C02).
section_moves.transferable_principle: For any stress-shielding metric, report numerator/denominator, spatial statistic, reference state, uncertainty, and what positive, zero, and negative values physically mean.
section_moves.failure_mode: A lower or negative surrogate must not be labeled beneficial without stability and tissue-response evidence.

author_reported: Pure axial 800 N loading, simplified cylindrical tibia, and a 1 mm non-contact plate-bone configuration limit interpretation to relative trends (S014:C02-S014:C03).
reader_identified: No experimental calibration or validation of materials, construct stiffness, fracture-gap motion, strength, fatigue, screw fixation, or SSF.
Incomplete optimization-contract reporting and no proof of global or robust optimum.
No uncertainty/sensitivity for multiaxial load, anatomy, contact, screw preload, callus properties, fracture, or AM anisotropy.
Manual manufacturability correction lacks quantitative geometric rules, printing, metrology, or mechanics.
Stress/strain directionality across plate, bone, and callus is not always reconciled with the load-sharing objective.
Healing weeks are assigned scenarios, not observed time points.
likely_bias_direction: Single-load optimization favors a light geometry that may be unsafe in bending/torsion/fatigue.
Surrogate-to-healing language overstates biological and clinical benefit.
Selective emphasis on favorable SSF may hide fracture-stability and overloading trade-offs.
limitations.scope_boundary: The study supports relative numerical comparison of plate materials and volume-reduced geometries in one simplified axial locked-plate construct; it does not establish a manufactured device, fatigue safety, biological remodeling, healing acceleration, or clinical recovery.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Write implant topology optimization as a complete objective-constraint-variable-load-manufacturing-convergence contract before using the word optimal.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: Three retained-volume cases under one load do not prove a general optimum.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Treat raw topology, reconstructed CAD, printed geometry, and tested construct as four separate validation states and quantify loss at each transition.
writing_capability_candidates.manuscript_use: Topology reconstruction, AM Methods, and validation Results.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: An edited CAD rerun is not manufacturing validation.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Define stress-shielding proxies with reference, spatial statistic, sign, load-sharing trade-off, and biological-validation boundary.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: A favorable FE SSF does not measure bone resorption, healing, or function.

critical_weaknesses: One simplified axial model and incomplete optimization specification.
SSF and assigned healing scenarios are overextended to functional recovery.

summary_zh: 这是一项纯数值材料筛选与拓扑优化研究。作者在简化圆柱胫骨、50%愈合骨痂、板骨间隙1 mm和单一800 N轴向载荷下比较金属、梯度材料和PEEK-CF骨板，再用SIMP保留75%、50%或25%体积。TOPO25在同一模型中呈现较轻和较低SSF，并在手工加厚/修正后重新FE；但这只验证了修正CAD在该模型中的响应，不是打印或力学验证。所谓第3–4周或第9周SSF来自预设骨痂参数，不能写成纵向愈合预测。Skill将据此强制要求：先给完整优化合同；把raw topology、重构CAD、as-built和实测构件分层；定义SSF参考和正负号；并把应力遮挡代理与骨重塑、愈合及功能恢复分开。
reader_notes: Primary Codex reader reviewed every non-reference section, material and topology comparison, corrected geometry, SSF definition, assumed healing trajectory, and limitations.
The automatic experimental-mechanical cue is incorrect; no physical experiment was performed.
The strongest transferable lesson is topology-contract and reconstruction-loss reporting, not evidence of clinical benefit.
